## Technical Corrections to This Historical Draft

This source is retained for audit history and is excluded from the production reading path. The corrections below govern its interpretation; the original wording is preserved separately.

LQR is an exact optimal-control solution for a declared linear system with an appropriate quadratic cost and the stated horizon/boundary conditions. Applying it along a nonlinear nominal motion solves a local model; shrinking perturbations does not turn every constrained nonlinear optimum into LQR or prove finite-region stability.

A value Hessian is a contraction metric only when it has the required uniform positive-definiteness and decay properties. A local optimum or lower rollout cost is not sufficient. Feedforward corrections, constraints and nonlinear rollout validation also matter in trajectory optimization. See the canonical control article linked above and [contraction conditions](../../../tangent-hyperplanes-series/part-5-contraction.html).

Current reading path: [Canonical Series Article](/articles/tangent-hyperplanes-series/part-3-control.html).

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true" title="Historical Draft: Superseded Wording"}

## Control in the Tangent Space

Optimal control operates locally in the tangent hyperplane.

## Linear Quadratic Regulation

LQR computes optimal policies assuming local linear dynamics
and quadratic costs.

This assumption is exact in the limit.

:::
